newsitem.title: USA: Clinton defends aides under financial scrutiny.
newsitem.headline: Clinton defends aides under financial scrutiny.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Friday stood by his selections of Anthony Lake to be CIA director and Samuel Berger as his national security adviser, saying he saw nothing "disqualifying" in questions raised about their personal finances.

"I will take full responsibility for whatever happens here," Clinton said at a news conference. "I am fully aware of the status of the issues here regarding Mr. Berger and Mr. Lake," both of whom are under Justice Department investigation for having failed to sell investments when told to do so to avoid any conflict of interest during service in Clinton's first term.
"I am convinced that nothing they did was in any way disqualifying," Clinton said.

Lake, Clinton's first-term national security adviser, and Berger, Lake's deputy who has been promoted to succeed him, are both under scrutiny for failing to sell large blocs of stock as soon as it was recommeded they do so. Both eventually did, and the delays have been described as oversights.

Berger's presidential advisory job requires no Senate confirmation but Lake does need Senate blessing to become head of the Central Intelligence Agency. He faces possible challenges on policy grounds as well as the financial matter.

On a related issue, Clinton agreed with a suggestion that people are becoming reluctant to accept high government appointments because of the fierce public scrutiny of their backgrounds. "There is no question that the climate has changed to the point that a lot of people don't want to fool with it anymore." he said.
